title: Modal verbs: potere, volere, dovere, sapere
description: Can, want, must and know how to — with an infinitive.
objectives: Conjugate potere, volere, dovere and sapere in the present.
Build modal + infinitive sentences, including negatives and pronouns.
Distinguish potere from sapere, and use vorrei for polite requests.

blocks.title: The second verb stays in the infinitive
blocks.text: A modal is followed directly by an infinitive, with no preposition: *Posso entrare? Voglio dormire. Devo studiare. So nuotare.*

blocks.title: Negation and pronouns
blocks.text: *non* goes before the modal: *Non posso venire.* An object or reflexive pronoun can go before the modal or be attached to the end of the infinitive (which drops its final -e): *Lo voglio vedere* = *Voglio vederlo*; *Mi devo alzare* = *Devo alzarmi*.

blocks.title: volere with a noun; vorrei
blocks.text: *volere* can also take a noun: *Voglio un gelato*. For polite requests use the conditional *vorrei* (I would like): *Vorrei un bicchiere d'acqua, per favore.* Saying *voglio* to a waiter sounds blunt.

blocks.caption: Two kinds of 'can'
rows: to know how to (a learned skill)
So nuotare. = I can (know how to) swim.
to be able / allowed to (circumstances, permission)
Oggi posso nuotare: il mare è calmo. = Today I can swim: the sea is calm.

blocks.text: Alone, *sapere* means to know a fact: *So che piove. Non lo so.* (To know a person or place is *conoscere*.)

examples.en: We have to go back home.
Can you swim? (Do you know how to swim?)

examples.it: Vorrei un bicchiere d'acqua, per favore.
examples.en: I'd like a glass of water, please.

mistakes.message: può needs the accent on the final o.

exercises.prompt: I know how to swim: ___ nuotare.

mistakes.message: posso = I am able / allowed (circumstances). For a learned skill use so.
conoscere means to know a person or place, not a skill.

exercises.prompt: Order: 'I have to get up early.' (pronoun attached to the infinitive)
exercises.explanation: The reflexive pronoun can attach to the infinitive: alzarmi. (Also correct: Mi devo alzare presto.)
non before the modal; infinitive venire.

exercises.prompt: Translate politely: I'd like a glass of water, please.
exercises.answer: Vorrei un bicchiere d'acqua, per favore.
accept: Vorrei un bicchiere di acqua, per favore.
exercises.explanation: vorrei is the polite form; d'acqua = di acqua.

summary: potere: posso, puoi, può, possiamo, potete, possono.
volere: voglio, vuoi, vuole, vogliamo, volete, vogliono.
dovere: devo, devi, deve, dobbiamo, dovete, devono.
sapere: so, sai, sa, sappiamo, sapete, sanno.
Modal + bare infinitive; pronouns before the modal or attached to the infinitive.
